reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the order and refund data myself, since payouts can't be recalled. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are in hand, but I haven't verified the refunds yet. I'll list the refunds to confirm they match what W2 reported before paying anyone.
The refund list matches W2's report exactly: orders 170, 172, and 175 with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 27298 matches my check: orders 170 and 173 total 28386, minus the 1088 refund on order 170. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 18633 matches my check: orders 171 and 174 total 18633, with no refunds on either. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net of 54502 matches my check: orders 172 and 175 total 64994, minus refunds 7535 and 2957 (10492). All three customers reconcile, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net of 18633 matches my check from the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net of 54502 matches my independent check (64994 in orders minus 10492 in refunds), so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded and each matched my independent check of orders minus refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
